## SETUP

Before building anything, we pick species that clear three checks:

1. **BirdFlow model exists.** Estimated flight paths need a fitted BirdFlow
   model. We started from the 60 vetted models in the June 2026 collection,
   because a species without a model can't get routes.
2. **Pacific Flyway use.** For every one of those 60 species, we measure the
   share of its population inside our study states during migration (Step 1).
   This is how we chose our species: by measured use of the flyway, not by
   guesswork.
3. **Quality for our season.** eBird scores every species' maps 0–3 for each
   season, and the BirdFlow model must cover that season (Steps 2–3).

The season comes from `R/config.R` (`SEASON_EBIRD`, `SEASON_BIRDFLOW`), so
nothing here is hard-coded to spring or fall. Switching seasons means changing
those two lines and re-running.

**Output:** `data/derived/species_selection.csv`, which notebooks 02 and 03 read.

```{r setup}
source(here::here("R", "config.R"))       # shared settings
source(here::here("R", "study_area.R"))   # study-area polygons

library(ebirdst)
library(BirdFlowR)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

## Step 1 · Rank all available models by Pacific Flyway use

```{r birdflow-index}
# Small index of every model in the current BirdFlow collection
# (default: the June 2026 release of 60 vetted models).
index <- load_collection_index()
```

For each species, we sum eBird's seasonal **proportion of population**
layer inside the study states. A value of 0.40 means about 40% of the
species' population is in our states, on average, during that migration
season. We compute both seasons so the season choice is also backed by data.

The first run downloads the 27 km files for all 60 species (small, cached
afterwards), so it takes 5–15 minutes. Later runs are fast.

```{r flyway-screen}
study_area <- study_states(merge = TRUE)

#' Share of a species' population inside the study states for one season.
#' Returns NA if the season failed eBird's review (no layer published) or
#' anything else goes wrong, so one bad species doesn't stop the loop.
flyway_share <- function(code, season) {
  tryCatch({
    ebirdst_download_status(code, pattern = paste0("_", EBIRD_RESOLUTION, "_"))
    r <- load_raster(code, product = "proportion-population",
                     period = "seasonal", resolution = EBIRD_RESOLUTION)
    if (!season %in% names(r)) return(NA_real_)
    terra::extract(r[[season]], vect(st_transform(study_area, crs(r))),
                   fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

ranked <- index |>
  select(common_name, species_code, model) |>
  mutate(
    spring_share = map_dbl(species_code, flyway_share, season = "prebreeding_migration"),
    fall_share   = map_dbl(species_code, flyway_share, season = "postbreeding_migration")
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(pmax(spring_share, fall_share, na.rm = TRUE)))

write_csv(ranked, file.path(PATHS$derived, "birdflow_models_ranked.csv"))

# Species with > 10% of their population in the study states in either season.
ranked |> filter(pmax(spring_share, fall_share, na.rm = TRUE) > 0.10)
```

**Result (team decision 10/25):** 16 species exceed 10%, then the shares drop
off sharply (the next species is about 6%; eastern species are near 0%). Spring
share was higher for 12 of those 16, consistent with western "looped"
migration (La Sorte et al. 2014) and Horton et al.'s (2019) finding of more
Pacific Flyway activity in spring. So spring is our core season, and we chose
our species from this list (check `CANDIDATE_SPECIES` in config.R).

## Step 2 · eBird quality for our season

`ebirdst_runs` ships inside the ebirdst package and has one row per species,
with each season's review score and date range. Its column names start with
the season name, so we build them from `SEASON_EBIRD`.

```{r ebird-quality}
ebird_check <- ebirdst_runs |>
  filter(species_code %in% CANDIDATE_SPECIES) |>
  select(
    species_code, common_name, scientific_name,
    # Review score 0–3 for our season (0 = failed review). We require 2+.
    season_quality = all_of(paste0(SEASON_EBIRD, "_quality")),
    # Species-specific season dates. The year (e.g. 2023) is the eBird data
    # version, not a real year: dates describe a TYPICAL year.
    season_start   = all_of(paste0(SEASON_EBIRD, "_start")),
    season_end     = all_of(paste0(SEASON_EBIRD, "_end"))
  ) |>
  # Some versions store the score as text ("3"); convert before comparing.
  mutate(season_quality = as.integer(season_quality),
         passes_ebird   = season_quality >= 2)

ebird_check
```

## Step 3 · BirdFlow model covers our season

The 2026 models are full-year, but older collections had season-only models
(e.g. `amewoo_prebreeding`), so we check rather than assume. Loading a model
downloads it once (tens to hundreds of MB) into BirdFlowR's cache.

```{r birdflow-season}
#' Does a species have a BirdFlow model covering our season?
#' Returns one row; tryCatch() turns "season not in this model" into FALSE.
check_birdflow_season <- function(code) {
  rows <- index |> filter(species_code == code)

  if (nrow(rows) == 0) {
    return(tibble(species_code = code, bf_model = NA_character_,
                  covers_season = FALSE, bf_note = "no model in collection"))
  }

  for (m in rows$model) {
    bf <- load_model(m)
    steps <- tryCatch(lookup_season_timesteps(bf, season = SEASON_BIRDFLOW),
                      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(steps) && length(steps) > 1) {
      return(tibble(species_code = code, bf_model = m, covers_season = TRUE,
                    bf_note = paste(length(steps), "weekly timesteps")))
    }
  }

  tibble(species_code = code, bf_model = paste(rows$model, collapse = ", "),
         covers_season = FALSE, bf_note = "model(s) don't cover this season")
}

bf_check <- map_dfr(CANDIDATE_SPECIES, check_birdflow_season)
bf_check
```

## Combine and save

```{r select}
selection <- ebird_check |>
  left_join(bf_check, by = "species_code") |>
  left_join(ranked |> select(species_code, spring_share, fall_share),
            by = "species_code") |>
  mutate(
    #  "routes + abundance" = full treatment (animated flight paths)
    #  "abundance only"     = eBird passes, but no BirdFlow model for this season
    #  "drop"               = eBird quality too low for this season
    use = case_when(
      passes_ebird & covers_season ~ "routes + abundance",
      passes_ebird                 ~ "abundance only",
      TRUE                         ~ "drop"
    )
  ) |>
  # Keep the priority order from config.R and cap the count.
  arrange(match(species_code, CANDIDATE_SPECIES)) |>
  mutate(selected = use != "drop" & cumsum(use != "drop") <= MAX_SPECIES)

selection |>
  select(common_name, season_quality, spring_share, fall_share, bf_model, use, selected)

write_csv(selection, file.path(PATHS$derived, "species_selection.csv"))
```

## If a species fails

All six should come back as `routes + abundance`. If one doesn't, swap in the
next-best species from Step 1's list (e.g. Calliope Hummingbird, Golden-crowned
Sparrow, etc.), update `CANDIDATE_SPECIES` in config.R with a dated comment, and
re-run this notebook.
